svg.aria-label: A permissions boundary shown as an intersection. On the left, the identity-based policy grants a set of actions. In the middle, the permissions boundary caps a set of actions and grants nothing. On the right, the effective permissions are the intersection of the two. Below, a note that a boundary allowing an action gives nobody that access on its own. At the bottom, four numbered routes that land outside the intersection: a resource-based policy naming the session ARN, a role passed to a service rather than assumed, service-linked roles which cannot carry a boundary, and a delegate able to edit the boundary policy itself.
svg.title: How a permissions boundary produces effective permissions, and the four routes that arrive outside the intersection
svg.text: A boundary is a ceiling, not a grant
Effective permissions are the intersection of two sets. Only one of the two sets can ever put an action into the result.
Identity-based policy
Grants. This is the only half
that can put an action in.
s3:* ec2:* iam:CreateUser
Permissions boundary
Grants nothing on its own.
Sets the maximum.
s3:* cloudwatch:* ec2:*
Effective permissions
Present in both sets. An explicit
deny in either removes it again.
s3:* ec2:* — and nothing else
Attach the boundary to an entity with no identity policy and the result is empty. iam:CreateUser is in the left set only, so it is denied.
Four routes that land outside the intersection
A resource-based policy names the session ARN
Permission granted directly to a session is not limited by an implicit deny in a permissions boundary.
The role is passed to a service, not assumed by the person
iam:PassRole hands a service a role whose own ceiling nobody set. The service acts, not the bounded entity.
Service-linked roles cannot carry one
You cannot apply a permissions boundary to a service-linked role. Whatever a service creates is outside the scheme.
The boundary document is itself an editable policy
A delegate who can publish a new version of the boundary policy raises their own ceiling in one API call.
Each route is documented AWS behaviour, not a defect. A boundary bounds identity-based policy, and only identity-based policy.
